"""Helpers shared by the movement generators. Melodies, chords and orchestration are chosen by hand in the
generators; these helpers only spell out repeated accompaniment figures. Sources are written in C-based keys
and transposed up a minor second by the build (@transpose +m2), so they sound in D flat."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'kit/')
from build import transpose
J = ' | '.join
# written chord -> bass, viola pair, second-violin pair, harp low arpeggio, harp high arpeggio
CH = {
 'C6':  ('C,',   ('E', 'G'),   ('A', 'c'),   'C,G,C',      'EAc'),
 'Am7': ('A,,',  ('E', 'G'),   ('A', 'c'),   'A,,E,A,',    'CEG'),
 'F6':  ('F,,',  ('F', 'A'),   ('c', 'd'),   'F,,C,F,',    'Acd'),
 'D9':  ('D,',   ('^F', 'A'),  ('c', 'e'),   'D,A,D',      '^Fce'),
 'FM7': ('F,,',  ('F', 'A'),   ('c', 'e'),   'F,,C,F,',    'Ace'),
 'G9':  ('G,,',  ('F', 'A'),   ('B', 'd'),   'G,,D,G,',    'FAd'),
 'Em7': ('E,',   ('E', 'G'),   ('B', 'd'),   'E,B,E',      'GBd'),
 'Dm7': ('D,',   ('D', 'F'),   ('A', 'c'),   'D,A,D',      'FAc'),
 'Bb':  ('_B,,', ('D', 'F'),   ('_B', 'd'),  '_B,,F,_B,',  'DF_B'),
 'Ab':  ('_A,,', ('_E', '_A'), ('c', '_e'),  '_A,,_E,_A,', 'C_E_A'),
 'Gb':  ('_G,,', ('_D', '_G'), ('_B', '_d'), '_G,,_D,_G,', '_B,_D_G'),
 'C':   ('C,',   ('E', 'G'),   ('c', 'e'),   'C,G,C',      'EGc'),
}
def sh(pair):                      # 6/8 shimmer between two notes
    x, y = pair; return f'{x}{y}{x} {y}{x}{y}'
def L(vid, bars, pre=''): return f"{vid}: {pre}{J(bars)} |\n"
def acc68(chords, dyn='pp', harp=True, v2=True, cbpizz=True, first=''):
    """Shimmering violas (and second violins), held cellos, plucked basses, harp arpeggio in every bar."""
    t = L('va', [sh(CH[c][1]) for c in chords], f'{first}!{dyn}!')
    if v2: t += L('v2', [sh(CH[c][2]) for c in chords], f'!{dyn}!')
    t += L('vc', [CH[c][0] + '6' for c in chords], f'@arco !{dyn}!')
    cb = [transpose(CH[c][0], '-P8') for c in chords]
    t += L('cb', [f'{b}3 z3' for b in cb], '@pizz !p!') if cbpizz else L('cb', [f'{b}6' for b in cb], f'@arco !{dyn}!')
    if harp:
        t += L('hl', [CH[c][3] + ' z3' for c in chords], '!mf!') + L('hu', ['z3 ' + CH[c][4] for c in chords], '!mf!')
    return t
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Movement I. usage: gen1.py [sections]  (default: all)"""
import pathlib, sys
from common import *
X = "E3 G2 A | c3 d2 e | d3 c2 A | G6".split(' | ')                       # the call
T1 = "g3 a2 c' | e'3- e'2 d' | c'2 a c'2 e' | d'6 | g3 a2 c' | e'3 ^f'2 g' | e'2 d' c'2 a | g6".split(' | ')
T1c = ['C6', 'C6', 'Am7', 'F6', 'C6', 'D9', 'FM7', 'C6']
sec = []
sec.append('% The violas murmur on two notes over a held bass; the harp rises through the chord\n' + acc68(['C6'] * 4, v2=False, first='[M:6/8] '))
sec.append('% The call: cor anglais, then horn a fourth higher\n' + L('eh', X + ['z6'] * 4, '!f!') + L('hn', ['z6'] * 4 + [transpose(b, '+P4') for b in X], '!f!')
           + acc68(['C6', 'C6', 'Am7', 'C6', 'F6', 'F6', 'Dm7', 'C6']))
sec.append('% First theme: the flute, over shimmering strings and harp\n' + L('fl', T1, '!f!') + acc68(T1c))
sec.append('% The theme in the first violins and oboe, the flute floating above, horns holding the harmony\n' + L('v1', T1, '!mf!') + 'ob: = v1\n'
           + L('fl', "e'6 | g'6 | e'6 | a'6 | e'6 | ^f'6 | a'3 g'3 | e'6".split(' | '), '!mf!')
           + L('hn', "[EG]6 | [EG]6 | [EG]6 | [FA]6 | [EG]6 | [^FA]6 | [FA]6 | [EG]6".split(' | '), '!p!') + acc68(T1c, dyn='p'))
WT = ('@def WT\n' + L('eh', "E3 ^F2 ^G | _B3 c2 d | c3 _B2 ^G | ^F6".split(' | '), '!f!')
      + L('va', [sh(('C', 'D'))] * 4, '!pp!') + L('v2', [sh(('^F', '^G'))] * 4, '!pp!') + L('vc', ['_B,,6'] * 4, '!pp!') + L('cb', ['_B,,,3 z3'] * 4, '@pizz !p!')
      + L('hl', ['C,D,E, ^F,^G,_B,', 'z6', 'C,D,E, ^F,^G,_B,', 'z6'], '!mf!') + L('hu', ['z6', 'CDE ^F^G_B', 'z6', 'cde ^f^g_b'], '!mf!') + '@end\n')
sec.append('% The call bends into the whole-tone scale over a low pedal\n' + WT + '\n% The same a step higher\n@use WT +M2\n')
sec.append('% Whole-tone waves rise through the strings; a muted trumpet takes the head of the call\n'
           + L('v1', "cde ^f^g_b | c'_b^g ^fed | cde ^f^g_b | c'd'e' ^f'^g'_b'".split(' | '), '!mf!') + 'v2: = v1 -P8\n'
           + L('va', [sh(('E', '^G'))] * 4, '!mf!') + L('hn', "[CE]6 | [D^F]6 | [E^G]6 | [^F_B]6".split(' | '), '!mf!')
           + L('tp', "z6 | z6 | E3 ^F2 ^G | _B6".split(' | '), '!f!')
           + L('fl', ["e'^f'e' ^f'e'^f'"] * 2 + ["^g'_b'^g' _b'^g'_b'"] * 2, '!f!') + 'ob: = fl -P8\n'
           + L('vc', "C,6 | D,6 | E,6 | ^F,6".split(' | '), '!mf!') + 'bn: = vc\ncb: @arco = vc -P8\n'
           + L('hl', ['C,D,E, ^F,^G,_B,'] * 4, '!f!') + L('hu', ['cde ^f^g_b'] * 4, '!f!'))
tops = ["g'", "f'", "_e'", "_d'"]; mids = ["e'", "d'", "c'", '_b']; lows = ['c', '_B', '_A', '_G']
sec.append('% Climax: four major chords descend by whole steps, C, B flat, A flat, G flat (as written; a half step higher as heard)\n'
           + L('fl', [f'{n}6' for n in tops], '!ff!') + L('ob', [f'{n}6' for n in mids], '!ff!') + L('cl', "c'6 | _b6 | _a6 | _g6".split(' | '), '!ff!')
           + L('eh', "g6 | f6 | _e6 | _d6".split(' | '), '!ff!')
           + L('hn', "[EG]6 | [DF]6 | [C_E]6 | [_B,_D]6".split(' | '), '!ff!') + L('tp', "c6 | _B6 | _A6 | _G6".split(' | '), '!f!')
           + L('v1', [f'{n}{n}{n} {n}{n}{n}' for n in tops], '!ff!') + L('v2', [f'{n}{n}{n} {n}{n}{n}' for n in mids], '!ff!') + L('va', [f'{n}{n}{n} {n}{n}{n}' for n in lows], '!ff!')
           + L('vc', "C,6 | _B,,6 | _A,,6 | _G,,6".split(' | '), '!ff!') + 'bn: = vc\ncb: = vc -P8\n' + L('tm', "C,3 C,3 | z6 | z6 | z6".split(' | '), '!f!')
           + L('hl', [CH[c][3] + ' ' + CH[c][3] for c in ['C', 'Bb', 'Ab', 'Gb']], '!ff!') + L('hu', [CH[c][4] + ' ' + CH[c][4] for c in ['C', 'Bb', 'Ab', 'Gb']], '!ff!'))
sec.append('% The sound thins to a dominant ninth\n' + acc68(['G9', 'G9'], dyn='pp'))
sec.append('% The theme returns in violins in octaves with the flute; clarinet and horns fill the harmony\n' + L('v1', T1, '!f!') + 'v2: = v1 -P8\nfl: = v1\n'
           + L('cl', [sh(CH[c][2]) for c in T1c], '!mf!') + L('hn', "[EG]6 | [EG]6 | [EG]6 | [FA]6 | [EG]6 | [^FA]6 | [FA]6 | [EG]6".split(' | '), '!mf!')
           + acc68(T1c, dyn='mf', v2=False))
sec.append('% Coda: the call in the horn, the theme\'s first notes in the flute, and the chord fades\n'
           + L('hn', X + ['z6'] * 6, '!f!') + L('fl', ['z6'] * 4 + "g3 a2 c' | e'6 | z6 | z6 | z6 | !fermata!z6".split(' | '), '!mf!')
           + L('v1', ['z6'] * 8 + ["e'6", "!fermata!e'6"], '!pp!')
           + acc68(['C6', 'C6', 'Am7', 'C6', 'C6', 'C6', 'C6', 'C6'], dyn='pp', harp=False)
           .replace('va: !pp!', 'va: !pp!').rstrip('\n').replace(' |\ncb', ' |\ncb')
           + '\n' + L('hl', ['C,G,C z3', 'z6', 'A,,E,A, z3', 'z6', 'C,G,C z3', 'z6', 'C,G,C z3', 'z6'], '!mf!') + L('hu', ['z3 EAc', 'z6', 'z3 CEG', 'z6', 'z3 EAc', 'z6', 'z3 eac\'', 'z6'], '!mf!'))
# the last two bars of the coda: every string part holds its chord tone
END = {'v1': None, 'v2': ['A6', '!fermata!A6'], 'va': ['G6', '!fermata!G6'], 'vc': ['C,6', '!fermata!C,6'], 'cb': ['C,,3 z3', '!fermata!C,,3 z3'], 'hl': ['C,G,C z3', '!fermata![C,G,]6'], 'hu': ["z3 eac'", "!fermata![Ec]6"]}
def finish(text):
    out = []
    for l in text.split('\n'):
        vid = l.split(':')[0]
        if vid in END and END[vid] and l.count('|') == 8:
            l = l.rstrip().rstrip('|').rstrip() + ' | ' + ' | '.join(END[vid]) + ' |'
        out.append(l)
    return '\n'.join(out)
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else len(sec)
head = '''@label I. Très modéré
@note NOTE
@meter 6/8
@tempo "Très modéré" 3/8=46
@key Db
@transpose +m2
'''
note_full = "D flat major. Murmuring violas and harp; a call for cor anglais and horn; a floating theme for the flute; a middle section that bends the call into the whole-tone scale and rises to four descending major chords; the theme returns and the call closes the movement."
note_part = "Work in progress. D flat major. Murmuring violas and harp; a call for cor anglais and horn; a floating theme for the flute."
body = sec[:n]
if n == len(sec): body[-1] = finish(body[-1])
text = head.replace('NOTE', note_full if n == len(sec) else note_part) + '\n'.join(body)
lines = text.rstrip('\n').split('\n'); i = len(lines) - 1
import re
while i >= 0 and re.match(r'^\w+: ', lines[i]): lines[i] = re.sub(r'\|\s*$', '|]', lines[i]); i -= 1
pathlib.Path('src/m1.mw').write_text('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
EOF

A symphony Debussy did not write

Debussy left no orchestral symphony; the nearest things are an early symphony movement for piano four hands and the three “symphonic sketches” of La Mer. This homage is a short symphony in D flat in four movements, about nine minutes long ({TOTAL} in the site’s playback). It borrows his habits more than his forms: melodies on five-note and whole-tone scales, chords that slide in parallel, shimmering accompaniments, solo woodwind, harp, and themes that return in later movements.

The score has fifteen staves at sounding pitch: flute, oboe, cor anglais, clarinet, bassoon, horns, trumpets, timpani, harp (two staves) and strings.

F · A♭ B♭ · D♭ E♭ F

The call: six rising notes of the five-note scale, which then fall back.

I. Très modéré

D flat major · 6/8 · 64 bars · about {DUR_i}

Violas murmur on two notes over a held bass while the harp rises through the chord. The cor anglais plays the call, and the horn repeats it a fifth lower. The flute has the first theme, a floating tune with one raised note (the Lydian fourth); the first violins and oboe repeat it with the flute above. The tempo quickens a little as the call bends into the whole-tone scale over a low pedal; whole-tone waves rise through the strings with a muted trumpet, and the climax is four major chords descending by whole steps. After two held-back bars the theme returns in the violins with the cor anglais playing the call beneath it, and the horn’s call closes the movement.

II. Assez vif et léger

E flat Dorian · 9/8 · 64 bars · about {DUR_ii}

A light dance for the oboe, then for flute and clarinet, over harp triads and plucked basses. A second idea has the strings moving in parallel fourths over a stepwise bass; the full orchestra takes it up with a muted trumpet tapping the rhythm. In the middle the cor anglais has a long melody over harp and held strings, repeated by flute and first violins. The dance returns in plucked violins, then oboe and clarinet, the second idea comes once more, and the tune breaks into fragments before a last plucked chord.

III. Lent et expressif

B flat minor · 4/4 · 26 bars · about {DUR_iii}

The strings move in parallel seventh chords, down the scale and back up. The flute plays a long arabesque over harp and held strings. The chords return with the cor anglais singing the arabesque’s first phrases over them, the flute floats above the second half, and the movement ends on a soft minor chord with an added ninth.

IV. Animé

D flat major · 6/8 · 84 bars · about {DUR_iv}

Over a quick shimmer the clarinet recalls the call. The main theme is a broad five-note tune, first in horns and cor anglais, then in trumpets, flute and oboe. The first movement’s theme returns in the violins and then in the woodwind with the call in the horns beneath it. The whole-tone music of the first movement comes back, rises twice, and reaches the same four descending chords. The main theme then fills the full orchestra, twice, the second time a step higher, and in a faster coda trumpets and horns broaden the call over the full shimmer before a five-note rush upward and the last chord.

Influences, and what is not quoted

  • No melody is quoted from Debussy or anyone else.
  • La Mer is the main model: themes shared between the first and last movements, a broad brass tune in the finale, and an opening call given to the cor anglais. In La Mer a call for cor anglais and muted trumpet plays the same role; the notes here are different, but the kinship is deliberate.
  • The cor anglais solos and the parallel chords of the slow movement follow “Nuages”; the muted trumpet tapping a rhythm in the second movement follows the distant procession in “Fêtes”; a long flute solo over harp recalls the Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune, though this arabesque is modal and not chromatic.
  • Whole-tone passages and chords moving in parallel are found throughout his piano Préludes and orchestral music. Five-note melodies reflect his interest in the gamelan he heard in Paris in 1889.
  • The four-movement plan with a separate slow movement is not Debussy’s; his orchestral works favour three panels. It was chosen because the request was for a symphony.

How it was written and revised

  • The melodies, the chord of every bar, the scoring of each section and the plan of each movement were chosen by hand. Small programs then spell out the repeated accompaniment figures (the shimmer between two notes, the harp arpeggios, the held and plucked basses) from the chord plan. The music was written in easier keys a half step lower and transposed by the build, so every note in the published score is at sounding pitch in D flat.

  • Balance: each of the fifteen parts was rendered alone, first for the opening and then for all four movements. The harp and the solo winds were lowered after the first measurement, and the flute and harp were lowered again in the finale’s loud passages after the second. The final version was not measured part by part again.
